gappers.catalyst: No Intuitive Machines news on Nov 26-27; a 24.75%-shorted space name bouncing off its $8.01 52-week low with the tape. Last items: NASA $10B lunar program slot (Nov 9), Q3 beat (Nov 12, -$0.02 vs -$0.11 est), Mizuho initiation at $15 (Nov 24).
gappers.catalyst_detail: Intuitive Machines published nothing on Nov 26 (market closed, Thanksgiving) or Nov 27. The last company-specific items are a NASA award giving it a slot in a $10 billion lunar program (Nov 9) and a Q3 report on Nov 12 that beat on EPS (-$0.02 vs -$0.11 estimated). Against that, the sell-side spent November cutting: Roth $30->$20, Canaccord $39->$38, B. Riley $43->$34, Keybanc $38->$30, and Mizuho's Nov 24 initiation came in at just $15 versus a $22.93 consensus. The stock closed Nov 25 at $9.14, 22.7% above its $8.01 52-week low and 48.2% below its 200-day SMA.
gappers.why: Short-squeeze mechanics on sector beta, not news. With 24.75% of float short and 3.09 days to cover, a 2.2% QQQ move forces covering in the most crowded space shorts; that is what lifts a stock sitting a fifth above its 52-week low. No new information about Intuitive Machines reached the market.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day bounce. The gap is only 0.57 ATR against a 12.3% ATR - just over half a normal daily range - and pre-market volume of 431K is 4.1% of its 10.6M 20-day average, so there is no participation behind it. Sector read-through is total: PL +6.13%, BKSY +5.82%, RDW +5.09% and RKLB +5.21% all moved with it, which confirms beta over thesis. Price remains 48.2% below the 200-SMA and 19.3% below the 50-SMA.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The underlying catalyst set is structural - a NASA slot in a $10B lunar program and a Q3 EPS beat - and aerospace/defense sits in the Industrials leg of the rotation table; but today's move is pure beta, so the thesis is a watch item, not an entry.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing - 0 open positions and 0/3 weekly trades used - so the true cost is one of three weekly slots. Within today's list its only real competitor is BE, which has the same improving-fundamentals-with-compressing-multiple shape at far larger scale, so BE ranks ahead. On R:R this is the most achievable name here: a 1-ATR stop is 12.3% ($8.62, just above the $8.01 52-week low) and needs only a +25% target of $12.28, essentially the $12.18 50-SMA, against a $22.93 consensus - so 2:1 clears at a sane stop. It still fails the 200-SMA long-bias filter by 48.2%, and the mandatory 10% trailing GTC stop sits 0.81 ATR away, inside one normal day. Research only.

gappers.catalyst: No Nebius news on Nov 26-27. Nov 25 was negative: a death cross formed as Microsoft reassessed neocloud projects and Meta explored selling excess AI compute, and the stock fell near its $73.52 52-week low.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius published nothing on Nov 26-27. Its most recent coverage is actively bearish: on Nov 25 Benzinga reported a death cross (50-SMA crossing below the 200-SMA) as Microsoft reassessed neocloud projects and Meta explored selling excess AI compute capacity, and separately that the stock had fallen near its 52-week low. On Nov 22 it was grouped with CoreWeave and IREN as neoclouds getting 'oversold as AI bubble fears rise'. Q3 (Nov 12) was a large headline beat (+$0.30 vs -$1.11 est, +127.5%), yet four brokers cut targets the next day, DA Davidson halving $250->$125. Consensus is still $218.90 against a $91.30 price - a gap that reflects stale targets, not upside.
gappers.why: Leveraged beta plus the highest short interest on the list (25.61% of float, only 1.72 days to cover - the fastest-covering crowd here). A capex-heavy neocloud is a high-duration proxy on AI sentiment and funding costs, so it falls hardest on margin warnings and bounces hardest on risk-on. Today's move is the bounce leg, with no Nebius-specific input.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day spike, and it is the weakest signal on the list. The gap is 0.37 ATR against an 18.6% ATR - barely a third of a normal session for this name. Pre-market volume of 1.71M is 5.1% of its 33.5M average. A confirmed death cross is in place and price is 49.2% below the 200-SMA and 47.6% below the 50-SMA. Read-through across the neocloud group is complete, so nothing here is Nebius-specific.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A headline-free bounce off a 52-week low inside a confirmed death cross, with the two most recent news items (Microsoft reassessing neoclouds, Meta reselling compute) both cutting against demand. Nothing structural has been repaired.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing at 0 positions, but would spend a weekly slot on the worst risk/reward on the list. 2:1 cannot clear at a sane stop: a 1-ATR stop is 18.6% wide ($74.31, effectively sitting on the $73.52 52-week low), demanding a +37% target near $125 for 2:1. Worse, the mandatory 10% trailing GTC stop is only 0.54 ATR away - about half a normal day's range - making it the most certain noise stop-out here. Fails the 200-SMA filter by 49.2%.

gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day bounce likely to mean-revert. The gap is 0.55 ATR on a 12.2% ATR, and pre-market volume of 160.6K is just 2.6% of its 6.25M average - among the thinnest here. Price is 53.1% below the 200-SMA and only 18.4% above a 52-week low set days ago, so there is almost no structural cushion beneath it. ONDS +5.66% confirms the drone/battery group is moving as one.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The $75M defense grant is structural but two months stale, and the most recent company event was a Q3 miss that sent the stock to a 52-week low. A thin bounce on no news is not a regime change.

gappers.catalyst_detail: Bloom Energy published nothing on Nov 26-27, and the two most recent news items are both negative: on Nov 25 the stock fell after Hunterbrook Media alleged Chinese scandium supply routes, compounding AI-market weakness and tariff pressure, and on Nov 24 it slid with the broader AI selloff. Fundamentally it is the strongest name here - Q3 (Oct 22) beat at $0.94 vs $0.65 estimated, Barclays upgraded on Nov 3, and consensus sits at $241.41 with RBC at $335. But the price has collapsed from a $351.28 52-week high to $152.89, and at a 92.66 P/E the multiple is still the binding risk.

AI-power names are being repriced by the group's discount rate, not by Bloom's results: peers confirm it, with GEV +3.39%, SMR +6.34% and XE +5.30% on the same print. Nothing about Bloom changed overnight.
gappers.impact: Best fundamentals here, still not a tradeable setup. The gap is 0.51 ATR on a 13.1% ATR, and pre-market volume of 588K is 3.3% of its 18.0M average. Sector read-through is explicit across fuel-cell and nuclear peers (GEV +3.39%, SMR +6.34%, XE +5.30%, INIO +4.52%). At 26.8% below the 200-SMA this is the shallowest breach on the list - and still a fail. The stock has round-tripped violently inside six sessions; in a 13%-ATR regime a 7% gap carries no information.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: AI/data-center power is a durable demand regime aligned with the Industrials/Technology leg of the rotation table, Q3 beat at $0.94 vs $0.65, and consensus sits at $241.41 versus $163.90 - worth a multi-day swing IF it reclaims the 200-SMA and clears Confluence.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace at 0 positions, and of today's ten this is the one thesis that survives the gap fading, so a weekly slot costs least here - but it is premature. The binding constraint is the mandatory 10% trailing GTC stop at 0.76 ATR - noise stops it out before the thesis can resolve. Correct action is WATCH with a trigger on reclaiming the $224.04 200-SMA on above-average volume, then re-check Confluence via /trade.

At $9.68 it is 23.8% above its $7.82 52-week low and 48.6% below its 200-day SMA.

gappers.impact: The least reliable print on the list and the most likely to mean-revert. Pre-market volume of 27,730 shares is 0.8% of its 3.35M 20-day average, and the prior session's volume was itself 0.77x average - below normal on both measures, the clearest non-confirmation here. The gap is 0.44 ATR against a 14.3% ATR. Price is 48.6% below the 200-SMA and 43.3% below the 50-SMA, with four straight earnings misses behind it.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Four consecutive earnings misses, a -233% Q3 surprise and targets cut from $40 to $22 give no durable thesis; the Dec 3 Investor Day is an event to watch, not a reason to hold through a fade.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing at 0 positions, but is strictly dominated by LUNR (same drone/defense-adjacent beta, a Q3 beat instead of a -233% miss, and a tighter ATR). 2:1 is not credibly clearable: a 1-ATR stop is 14.3% ($8.30, only 6% above the $7.82 52-week low) and would need a +29% target of $12.46 - straight into overhead supply well below the $17.07 50-SMA, with Needham having just cut $40->$22. Combined with 0.8%-of-average pre-market volume, this is the lowest-quality setup on the list.
